title: Antony Waste Handling Cell Ltd - 543254 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Antony Waste FY26 operating revenue rose 9% to Rs.920 crores; Q4 revenue up 14% to Rs.254 crores with EBITDA margin ~22%, order book at record Rs.18,000 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 marked 25 years of operations, with a maiden dividend of Rs.0.50 per share recommended. Volumes grew strongly: total MSW managed rose 15% to 5.69 million tons, and Q4 processing volumes jumped 32% to 1.15 million tons. Revenue growth was 9% for the year and 14% in Q4, with EBITDA margin held near 22% for both periods, though reported PAT was Rs.92 crores and Q4 PAT of Rs.37 crores was flattered by a Rs.24 crore one-time income in the prior-year base. Management reiterated 15-20% revenue CAGR over five years, citing the record order book and two large AP WTE projects.

financial_highlights.change: PAT up ~20% YoY adjusted for Rs.24 crore one-time income in FY25
Up ~67% YoY adjusted for one-time income in Q4 FY25

segments.name: C&T (Collection & Transportation)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.646 crores (+11%); Q4 Rs.160 crores (+14%). C&T volumes grew ~9% to 2.12 million tons in FY26. Two new Mumbai BMC C&T contracts are expected to be a larger part of the future order book.

segments.name: Processing
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.274 crores (+5%); Q4 Rs.94 crores (+15%). Processing volumes rose ~19% to 3.6 million tons in FY26 and 32% to 1.15 million tons in Q4, driven by biomining and MRF utilisation. Processing is ~60% of the Rs.18,000 crore order book per management.

segments.name: WTE (Waste-to-Energy)
segments.commentary: PCMC WTE delivered 69.3 million units of green power in FY26; plant PLF was 56% for the year after ~90 days of shutdown, and ~86% post maintenance. Two AP WTE projects with JFE Engineering are expected to contribute revenue after FY29.

segments.name: C&D recycling
segments.commentary: FY26 C&D revenue only ~Rs.9 crores, below expectations. Volumes reached 480-520 tons/day from February vs 280-300 tons/day in prior eight months; management guides ~Rs.18-20 crores for FY27.

segments.name: RDF / EPR
segments.commentary: Record RDF sales of 177,000 tons (+20%). EPR: nearly 20% of allotted credits monetised in first year of PCMC WTE operations; Rs.2.2 crores recognised so far, which management says could reach ~10% of PCMC WTE revenue once quantified.

guidance_outlook: 15-20% revenue CAGR over the next 5 years, backed by the Rs.18,000 crore order book and two AP WTE projects.
Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 20-22%; management says contractual escalation (100% of revenue per management) keeps margins in this band.
Incremental capex ~Rs.750 crores, mainly for Atkoli processing, two AP WTE projects and two Mumbai BMC C&T contracts; ~40% in FY27-28 and ~60% in FY28-29 per management.
AP WTE projects expected to contribute revenue post FY29.
Statutory effective tax rate assumption of 25% for group companies.
Expects C&D volumes to keep rising; current-year C&D revenue assumed at Rs.18-20 crores.
capex_capacity: PCMC WTE: 69.3 million units generated in FY26; ~86% PLF post maintenance shutdown.
Approx. 90 days of planned and reparative shutdown in FY26 drove 56% annual PLF.
Two AP WTE projects with JFE Engineering as technology vendor under fixed-term cost contracts; total capex of Rs.650-700 crores to be booked as contract revenue over ~2-2.5 years.
New Mumbai BMC contracts: Rs.1,330 crores revenue over 7 years (~Rs.190 crores per year), per management correction on the call.
Atkoli processing project is part of incremental capex; C&D processing capacity utilisation rising after BMC rules mandating routing through authorised C&D units.
demand_pricing: Volume growth: total MSW managed up 15% to 5.69 million tons in FY26; Q4 MSW handled up 23% to 1.67 million tons.
CIDCO biomining (fixed-term contract) is ~22% of volumes in Q4; non-CIDCO biomining revenue up ~8%, which management calls the underlying growth rate.
Escalation: contractual tariff escalation is built into contracts; delays in recognition were due to absence of standing committees and elected members, now resolved per management.
Labour code minimum wage change impact estimated at only Rs.5.2 crores across the book.
Auto tire recycling and scrapping: institutional demand below expectations; management is waiting before investing capital.
Click2Clean (B2B pest-control, recyclables, housekeeping) is a new small revenue line; clients include P.N. Gadgil, Asian Paints, Suntory Wines and Beams.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company sustain margins given rising fuel, additive and minimum wage costs, and how will working capital and debt fund the WTE ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt/equity is 0.3x, leaving room to borrow; ratings are A- at key subsidiary and BBB+ at listed entity; cost of borrowing sub-10%. All revenue has escalation built in; delays in realisation are acknowledged by clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume growth not translate into revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume jump was mainly from fixed-term CIDCO biomining contract, which is ~22% of Q4 volumes; non-CIDCO biomining revenue grew ~8%.

qa_highlights.question: What was the EPR credit monetisation value?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs.2.2 crores recognised for FY25-eligible credits; management expects this to rise to ~10% of PCMC WTE revenue once the pattern is established.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term debt fall and what drove the paydown?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash flow from operations before working capital was ~Rs.220 crores; Rs.93 crores total financing impact used to repay debt.

qa_highlights.question: Split of order book, capex needed and size of Mumbai contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book split ~60% processing and 40% C&T. Incremental capex ~Rs.750 crores for processing, AP WTE and BMC contracts. Mumbai BMC contracts Rs.1,330 crores over 7 years (corrected from an earlier misstatement of Rs.1,000 crores over 10 years).

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin soften and why did employee and other expenses rise ~19% and ~17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Wage inflation and headcount growth raised employee costs; other expenses rose on RDF transport (177,000 tons sold) and hiring. Margin softness from delayed monsoon-hit C&D volumes and extra vehicles at Nagpur, Noida and PCMC.

risks_watch: Delayed escalation recognition and client payment timing could widen working capital and reported margin gaps.
Rising fuel, additive and labour costs; management says Labour Code impact is only Rs.5.2 crores but margins are under pressure y/y.
Mumbai WTE remains unresolved at Bombay High Court; proposal from corporation awaited.
Bhiwandi arbitration: Rs.15 crores settlement due within 3 months in Q1 FY27 (9% interest on delay); remaining arbitration matters open.
Tax rate normalisation: FY26 included Rs.19 crore tax reversal (one-time items); 25% ETR assumed going forward.
AP WTE revenue contribution is only expected post FY29, so growth is back-ended; C&D and EPR revenue remain small.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, balance sheet and growth targets, with frank acknowledgement of soft C&D and auto-tire recycling demand. Management was cautious on near-term margin and cash-collection timing, and a few answers were corrected on the call (Mumbai contract size, PAT adjustment context).
key_quotes: We remain confident of delivering 15% to 20% revenue CAGR over the next 5 years, backed by a record Rs.18,000 crores order book, 2 large -scale WTE projects in Andhra Pradesh and expanding EPR platform and India secured tailwind in urban -based infrastructure, all while deepening our sustainability impact and creating long-term value for all our stakeholders.
All my projects, 100% of my revenue has escalation built into the system.
So, there might be a delay in realizing the cash flows, but the liability is acknowledged by the clients as per the tender conditions and is contractual, and that comes to us in due course of time.
